title: Capture decision accounts into Annals
summary: Observe eligible completed root user turns, classify every authority as decision or no-decision, and deliver deterministic immutable decision accounts to the dedicated Annals decisions library.
use_when: Post-activation decisions in completed local Codex root turns should be captured automatically.
Krisis observer coverage, pending Annals delivery, or a diagnosed failed observation should be inspected or recovered.
A missed Stop-hook correlation should be reconciled from normalized Conversations history.
do_not_use_when: Decision accounts should be searched or read after acceptance; use Annals.
A daily digest, review judgment, supersession graph, truth assessment, or current-force projection is wanted.
Raw transcripts, files, commands, tools, reasoning, or assistant-only proposals are intended as decision authority.
outcome: Complete durable decision or no-decision coverage for one eligible completed turn and, for each decision, an idempotently accepted immutable account in the configured Annals decisions library.
effects: The Stop hook durably records only a turn correlation; reconciliation may independently enqueue missed eligible completed turns.

One serial worker may submit one bounded two-level classification job through Nucleus, transactionally record coverage and a deterministic account outbox before acknowledgement, and invoke Annals acceptance for the oldest pending account.
After Annals accepts an account, Krisis retires its generated prose and body while retaining minimal correlation, authority anchor, digest, coverage, and acceptance receipt.
authority: A decision is an attributable user transition from practical openness to an explicit settlement constraining intended future behavior or state.
Only the exact cited user span supplies decision authority; assistant text may provide referential context, action, or result but never creates the decision.
Krisis owns capture and delivery state, Nucleus owns execution evidence, Conversations owns normalized source resolution, and Annals owns the accepted library.
success: Every eligible user authority in the admitted completed turn has exactly one durable decision or no-decision verdict.
Each decision account has a stable ID, exact authority quote and span, bounded statement and optional context/action/result, deterministic Markdown bytes, and a durable Annals outbox item.

Before classification, Krisis verifies and binds the exact Annals config path and expected library ID; delivery succeeds only when that target returns a matching created or replayed acceptance receipt.
failure_and_recovery: Ambiguous Nucleus admission resumes the same job and request digest; only positively terminal failure permits a successor, with one initial attempt plus two successors per scope.
Level zero may request one bounded level-one expansion; level one cannot request further context and oversized mandatory scope fails closed without truncation.
Annals outage leaves the exact account pending and retries delivery without reclassification; conflicting IDs, bytes, source identity, receipts, or dependency contracts fail closed.
Terminal observation retry and proven-unavailable unbound source abandonment require their explicit guarded recovery commands.
privacy: Nucleus receives at most 64 normalized messages and 262144 UTF-8 bytes under opaque aliases, with no real source IDs, paths, commands, tools, reasoning, approvals, file evidence, or web/local execution.
Krisis temporarily retains bounded accepted account prose until Annals acceptance; routine logs contain only bounded codes and opaque correlations.
Annals receives only the deterministic account Markdown and exact Source JSON anchor described by this contract.
does_not_authorize: Deploying or changing live schedules, Annals libraries, Nucleus registrations, authentication, or existing state.
Treating Nucleus output, assistant prose, observed action/result, or Annals acceptance as decision authority or truth.
Reading or mutating either product's SQLite database directly, widening classifier scope, or restoring retired digest/review behavior.

consumers.statement: The local current user and installed Krisis observer may capture post-baseline decisions into one explicitly configured dedicated Annals decisions library.
This capability is not a decision browser, daily digest, review queue, result tracker, or general transcript exporter.

preconditions.statement: Observation requires the write-once activation baseline, a uniquely resolved eligible completed root turn, compatible Conversations and Nucleus contracts, and private migration-compatible Krisis state.
Delivery requires an absolute Annals executable, an absolute dedicated-library config, and the exact 32-lowercase-hex expected library ID.

inputs.statement: Level zero contains every nonblank user authority in the completed turn, the nearest preceding assistant message for each when present, and at most the final assistant message; level one adds the newest prior normalized messages that fit.
The classifier submits exactly one verdict per authority and decision accounts containing an exact authority quote, statement, and optional context, action, and result with supporting aliases.
File-change evidence, raw items, real source IDs, paths, commands, tools, reasoning, approvals, web, and local execution are not classifier inputs.

outputs.statement: Krisis records complete binary authority coverage, stable decision IDs and exact spans, deterministic account SHA-256 digests, delivery state, Nucleus correlation, and matching Annals acceptance receipts.
Account Markdown contains ordered Decision, Authority, Context, Action, Result, and Source sections; absent context, action, or result is rendered as Unknown.
Krisis publishes no confidence, disposition, review, supersession, importance, current-force, enactment, truth, or longitudinal result field.

data_semantics.statement: Decision means an attributable user settlement constraining intended future behavior or state; no-decision is durable negative coverage for one authority.
Context, action, and result are observations available at capture time and do not affect eligibility; Unknown means not observed, not false or pending.
Annals created and replayed both mean the exact producer key and digest were accepted by the configured dedicated library.

identity_and_units.statement: Decision ID derives outside the model from host identity, canonical authority item identity, and the exact UTF-8 byte span; producer key equals decision ID.
Occurrence and completion times are Unix seconds with separately recorded timestamp precision; spans and scope limits are UTF-8 bytes.
Krisis publishes no pricing, usage, or accounting unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: A completed observation covers every admitted nonblank user authority exactly once and never silently truncates required context.
A decision remains pending end to end until Annals accepts it; acceptance becomes durable before generated account prose is retired.
No wall-clock bound from turn completion through classification or Annals acceptance is promised.

access.statement: Supported access is the local current-user krisis CLI, exact installed Stop hook, and release-pinned krisis/observer Clockwork runner; direct SQLite access is unsupported.
Cross-product calls use only the sealed Conversations, Nucleus protocol-v1, and Annals CLI interfaces with explicit configuration.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Validated coverage, stable identities, deterministic account bytes and digest, exact classifier call-argument digest, Nucleus correlation and receipt, and a target-bound outbox commit in one transaction before tool acknowledgement; identical redelivery is idempotent and conflict fails closed.
Observation is serial; one pending Annals delivery is attempted before new classification, so an outage never causes reclassification or parallel ownership.
After matching Annals acceptance, account body and generated prose may be discarded while minimal receipt, digest, authority anchor, coverage, and correlations remain.

operational_limits.statement: A scope contains at most 64 messages, 262144 aggregate UTF-8 bytes, and 100 accounts; quotes are at most 500 bytes and each generated field is 1 through 1000 bytes when present.
One observation has level zero and at most one level-one expansion; each scope has one initial attempt and at most two successors after positively terminal failure.
No throughput, queue-depth, storage-capacity, latency, or retention service-level objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Krisis provider 0.4.0 uses SQLite schema 4, account schema 1, capture rule krisis/decision-account-classification/1, and immutable Nucleus input/result schema version 1.
Legacy Decisions schema versions and classifier receipts remain decodable for migration and recovery, while digest and review commands and schedules remain disabled.
No future compatibility window, retention horizon, or release cadence is promised.

reliances.statement: Eligible turn discovery, exact normalized source resolution, message ordering, and timestamp precision rely on Conversations.
Bounded classification execution and durable tool transport rely on Nucleus without transferring decision or delivery authority.
Immutable account acceptance and dedicated-library identity rely on Annals; Krisis retains delivery authority until a matching receipt commits.
Periodic observer invocation relies on Clockwork immutable definitions and the krisis/observer binding.
Immediate Stop-hook correlation relies on the local Codex hook facility, for which no installed Chancery contract is declared.
